findings.title: [P2] Official verification searches the wrong provider page before reaching the corrected epoch predicate
findings.candidate_rule_id: D-03/D-05/D-07; scoped current-attempt repeated verification and discriminating regression evidence
findings.rationale:
Source-confirmed counterexample at the very official lifecycle used by the new bounded regression: the real normal create -> authorize -> options -> confirm -> subscribe/authenticated receipt flow selects phone 987654321 on the provider's second page, using after=fixture-page-1 at number-onboarding-flow.e2e-spec.ts:50-56. It reaches a persisted CONNECTED/RECEIPT_VERIFIED attempt with pairingEpoch=null and a channel with pairingEpoch=0; those assertions are at lines 74-87. The subsequent administrative verify calls at lines 89-90 invoke ChannelsService.verificar. That caller passes only WABA, phone ID and active scoped token to meta.confirmarNumero at channels.service.ts:287, omitting the page cursor. The unchanged fixture at helpers.ts:59-70 searches only its first returned page when after is absent. This excludes the chosen phone and returns null, so channels.service.ts:290 throws PROVIDER_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND before the transaction at lines 317-342 and before convergeReceiptVerifiedAttempt at line 337. This is an inference from exact local source control flow; this reviewer did not execute the request or observe its response code.

This is not only an unrealistic fixture condition. The production MetaHttpClient.confirmarNumero at meta.client.ts:121-127 checks the current scoped grant/WABA and then searches exactly one numerosDaWaba page using its optional after argument. numerosDaWaba limits a page to 100 (lines 105-118). An already authorized, durably owned selected phone outside the first current page therefore has the same conditional availability failure. The existing onboarding confirmation intentionally accepts an explicit page cursor; no such cursor is persisted or supplied by this verify caller. The page size of one in the fixture is a legitimate way to exercise that provider contract, not evidence that all production WABAs fail.

Why it is in this bounded review: it is fresh evidence at the same repeated-verification caller and the newly required official regression, rather than a reopening of the whole unchanged feature. The pagination behavior predates cp36b; the nullable helper does not introduce it. Nevertheless the delivered normal official repeated-verification behavior still cannot be accepted. Root expressly reported that the current frozen final-all run is still returning official [409,409], with its exact conflict code/root-cause diagnosis pending; I did not read that live log. The preserved complete pre-fix API RED also reports [409,409] versus [200,200] and ends at the status assertion. It does not record the official response codes. Consequently that authentic RED is not discriminating proof that this normal test reached, and failed because of, the old numeric epoch predicate. The unchanged page mismatch can produce the same RED both before and after the null-epoch correction. The old NUM-ADH-CP36-01 source mismatch has been removed correctly, but its behavioral/release closure is still unproved and the current official test remains an explicit blocking failure. No privilege escalation or cross-tenant write is demonstrated by this counterexample.
findings.suggested_action:
Keep this source snapshot and all raw RED artifacts intact. Under root-owned scope admission, resolve the official verify path's first-page assumption with a bounded provider-supported verification of the persisted selected phone under the current scoped grant and WABA ownership. Preserve the explicit page-specific onboarding confirmation, real credential use, exact phone comparison, grant/session revalidation, no HTTP inside DB transactions and the existing maximum request/time/lease budgets. Do not solve this by an unbounded WABA scan, global credential, trusting a submitted phone ID, accepting a missing provider resource, or changing the shared provider fake to return every phone. Any adapter path beyond the four frozen correction files needs explicit root admission before a serialized writer touches it; this review authorizes no code change.

Also make the null-epoch regression causal: use a genuine normal official lifecycle whose selected phone can be verified by the declared provider fixture, demonstrate that the pre-correction request actually reaches the epoch conflict (including its safe error code), and prove two successful post-fix verifications with unchanged completed attempt version, receipt, owner/currentAttempt and active credential metadata. Retain a separate explicit second-page verify case so isolating the epoch regression cannot conceal this newly demonstrated caller defect. Do not relabel the existing full status-only RED as an ATTEMPT_STALE reproduction or reconstruct missing details. The Evolution null negative and generation/state/epoch rollback fences must remain.

Preferred A is a narrow caller/adapter correction plus discriminating normal-lifecycle tests, followed by a new frozen package and the appropriate canonical validation and affected independent reviews. Effort is small to moderate; risk is bounded but requires preserving scoped resource proof and request budgets; blast radius is this official verification port/caller and its tests; maintenance and structural soundness improve by removing an implicit first-page precondition. B is to isolate the null-epoch test using a legitimately verifiable first-page lifecycle while retaining this pagination defect as an unresolved same-contract finding; that is lower effort for predicate proof but cannot close the observed page-two failure. C, accepting the still-failing normal lifecycle or weakening provider/epoch proof to make it green, does not meet D-03/D-05/D-07. Root owns final classification and the next admitted correction.

overall_assessment:
One material P2 blocks acceptance of the current delivered official repeated-verification behavior: NUM-ADH-CP36B-01. The original NUM-ADH-CP36-01 null-versus-zero predicate is corrected in the actual current source, but behavioral/release closure is pending because the required official regression is blocked earlier by a provider-page mismatch and the current final-all run is reported to still return 409. Do not accept this package or claim new GREEN from source inspection alone. No new P1 security/data-loss finding, exploitable authentication/tenant bypass, secret exposure, additional network call inside a transaction, or broad architecture shortcut was established by this bounded delta. This is a supplemental source recommendation, not a final review or whole-delivery/recovery acceptance.

Read the historical cp36-adherence-security result and independently matched its SHA256 6647e509bd021facbb6a2ae39c2f9b047eb5c0813168f49ef9ef39adb6cca870; it remains historical for its own hashes. Recomputed and rechecked all four current source digests against cp36b-review-source-freeze.json: helper ca8cb841fab2574866c3508ab41aa0a269608a20658db18840b2b89f0c281512; ChannelsService 0cf8f1936e4d4d8b912fae5cf6aaddd74d503eee5edcb8aaf61c11ca782f64cf; Evolution controller 12139a5b50b4dacf43492e038c91f006c9db999d0f6a76fd5d73e45ee987a041; flow test 2e06f82d138d4ce391a21eff17b32ddfc4ea7be45459cde80c994c05760ed0cb. No builds, tests, provider calls, runtime/DB inspection, private dotenv/.local-files/operator data access, broad Git blobs, Git/code/canon writes, goals or delegation were performed. Only this absolute raw result artifact is written and schema-validated.

Explicit disposition of NUM-ADH-CP36-01: receipt-attempt-convergence.ts:8 now requires number|null, rather than accepting omitted undefined. Both the conditional update and completed lookup retain pairingEpoch as an explicit equality predicate (lines 14,22). In Prisma's declared nullable Int model this represents the persisted null official value, rather than omitting the predicate or allowing an OR fallback. ChannelsService:336 chooses null only for the OFICIAL branch of the validated channel modality; NAO_OFICIAL keeps channel.pairingEpoch. The controller validates the two allowed modalities before the service call (channels.controller.ts:84-91); the service scopes its initial lookup by buId/type and locks a matching same-BU/provider durable identity (channels.service.ts:261-275). Thus this is trusted channel applicability, not a callback choosing the weaker epoch. Evolution continues to pass context.pairingEpoch, typed number, at evolution.controller.ts:130. The helper preserves exact ID and generation on both paths, the two existing pending states for promotion, one promotion version increment, and exact CONNECTED plus RECEIPT_VERIFIED for an already-completed no-write success. Wrong numeric epoch, null Evolution epoch, wrong generation and non-completed incompatible state/stage cannot enter that completed success. No operational-data normalization, schema/dependency change or generic null-or-number fallback is introduced. The old numeric-only source assumption is gone; root must retain the distinction between that static correction and the still-unaccepted normal-flow outcome.

Affected decision adherence, individually:
D-03 — The provider-specific attempt predicate is source-adherent: current attempt/generation applicability, CAS-style conditional promotion and no completed version bump remain. The corrected null contract agrees with official create/promotion, which leave attempt.pairingEpoch null (number-registration.service.ts:122-128,357-363; schema.prisma:210). No nonce/code reuse, new session path or HTTP within transaction is added. Repeated official behavior remains blocked before convergence as the finding details; no end-to-end D-03 closure is asserted.
D-05 — Registration, explicit registration mode, subscription and authenticated receipt sequencing are unchanged. The new official test uses the real BFF/AppModule/Prisma lifecycle and actual persisted null provenance, rather than fabricating a completed official attempt. However its verify lookup of a page-two number fails before applying the corrected convergence, so the official repeat requirement is not behaviorally satisfied on the current package. The no-false-CONNECTED rule is preserved; do not bypass resource validation to resolve the failure.

The current helper still requires exact numeric epoch for Evolution, and the added nullable fixture negative at flow test:712-715 checks ATTEMPT_STALE and no channel convergence. The existing temporary runtime recovery exception remains open until the corrected runtime and a fresh human exchange are accepted.
D-07 — Durable same-BU provider ownership, current channel/attempt, channel generation and applicable epoch continue to fence acceptance. Readiness still requires existing receipt and the observed applicable connection/subscription state. The exact completed lookup preserves attempt version; neither helper branch writes receipt, resource owner or credential. The page lookup defect prevents a valid explicit observation for some owned official resources, so the delivered official observation behavior is mixed. Persisted receipt/CONNECTED remains a last observation, not continuous health or a new exchange.
Other decisions are carried only where this correction leaves them untouched: D-01 has no new tenant/BU creation or canonical-phone overwrite; the existing locked current-phone check/CAS remains. D-02 has no SDK/OAuth journey or choice-of-number redesign; the new finding is at the reused verification read. D-04 retains the active channel-scoped credential resolver with generation/version AAD and no global-token fallback; this correction never exposes the credential or changes envelopes. D-08 adds no message/conversation/Typebot/realtime writer and does not change transactional deduplication or publication. D-09 adds no provider/runtime ownership change and provides no Railway/device proof. D-10 is preserved within this review by read-only source/Git use and a single output artifact; source push/deploy is not authorized. Unchanged full-feature decisions are not reaudited or newly certified. integrations-and-channels remains the module owner; its explicit official-null versus Evolution-exact-numeric paragraph matches the helper/caller correction. The new page mismatch is a concrete remaining same-caller behavioral inconsistency, not a reason to redesign the approved module.

Security/adversarial and concurrency assessment: examined the caller fences, not just the nullable helper. Administrative verify still authorizes ADMIN on the requested BU before modality validation, enforces the unofficial module gate and revalidates current session/user/grant around external reads (channels.controller.ts:84-91,107-113). The reservation locks provider identity -> BU -> channel, verifies managed lifecycle and obtains one bounded channel operation lease. The commit transaction requires that identity still point to the same channel and checks currentAttemptId/generation/channel epoch/lease token/unexpired lease against the locked current row (channels.service.ts:318-323). It checks the current canonical BU phone before writing own-number trust and conditionally connected status; a helper false throws in the same transaction, rolling those changes back. Provider reads and credential resolution happen outside that transaction; the finally block releases only the same generation/epoch/token lease. The null expected attempt epoch does not weaken the numeric channel epoch or lease fences.

Evolution authenticates the private header with a timing-safe equality check before provider identity lookup (evolution.controller.ts:25-38,69-75); external instance name is resolved through the durable provider-specific identity. Connection handling locks same identity/current channel/BU, then BU/channel, re-reads generation and numeric epoch and derives currentAttemptId from that locked channel (lines 117-130). Its ready condition still requires open, ownNumberVerified, matching verifiedEpoch and a receipt. An untrusted payload cannot choose an attempt ID, null epoch or BU owner for the helper. No new SQL interpolation pattern, injection/SSRF path, raw payload persistence, error text, secret sink, credential promotion or lock ordering is introduced. The exact small helper legitimately relies on its trusted fenced callers for tenant ownership; adding duplicate tenant parameters is not needed to resolve a new security defect. This review does not reclassify unchanged cancellation/event-order races or claim a new stress/race measurement. No new dependency/crypto behavior warrants claiming a fresh dependency or threat-intel audit.

Performance, elegance and structure: relative to the reviewed cp36 helper, cp36b changes a type and the caller's expected value, adding no database or external round trip. The shared helper's existing conditional update is ID-scoped, and only a miss adds one findFirst with the unique primary-key ID plus exact generation/epoch/state/stage while selecting ID alone. This is a bounded lookup under the existing locks, not list fan-out, a tenant-size scan or a newly justified index. The official first-page defect must not be corrected with an unbounded enumeration that violates the provider budget. No new PCV, latency/SLO, concurrency capacity or EPS measurement is asserted; older resolver/index samples do not measure this helper. A single Channels-domain convergence operation with Prisma.TransactionClient remains a simple faithful abstraction for the two callers. The explicit nullable expected epoch is clearer and more accurate than data normalization or an OR fallback; the completed branch makes no unnecessary version write. Elegance is acceptable for this correction, while overall structural/operational fit is mixed because the actual normal official caller still fails and the causal regression remains unproven. No future generic jobs, worker, schema or dependency architecture is justified.

Test/evidence quality and timing: the official test additions inspect actual post-lifecycle channel/attempt epochs and currentAttemptId, then request verification twice and intend to check receipt, completed version, owner and safe active-credential metadata (flow:77-102). This is substantively better than injecting a completed official fixture, and it avoids reading token/ciphertext into assertion output. Its page-two prerequisite currently prevents it reaching those post-verify assertions or proving the null fix. The Evolution negative assigns pairingEpoch=null only in a disposable PostgreSQL attempt after valid pairing/receipt and deliberately maintains the channel's numeric epoch; it requires 409 ATTEMPT_STALE and retained CONNECTING/no convergence, while preserving the earlier state/generation/epoch negatives. There is no production test flag or altered provider fake in these four changes. The negative covers the numeric pending-promotion predicate directly; the completed predicate's strict numeric equality is source-checked here, not separately runtime-proved by this null fixture.

The full pre-production-edit RED log is genuine preserved evidence, SHA256 b7a28b21c86b5cbfdfe167c084fa5ca9af645be3746749fc0bb7e79fa38fd445, ending RUNNER_EXIT=1 with 138 unit tests passed and 287 PostgreSQL tests passed/one official failure. The before-final-red manifest contains this same corrected test hash and the older numeric helper/caller hashes, while the after/freeze manifests identify the nullable correction; this distinguishes the genuine sequence from reconstructed history. The first raw RED's mistaken fixture final expectation and its correction are acknowledged in the packet; the second RED retains the Evolution null rejection and reports only the official status failure. This reviewer does not allege fabricated logs. Causal precision is narrower: [409,409] alone cannot identify ATTEMPT_STALE when the source first-page check can return another conflict before the helper. cp36b repairs the old missing-full-RED-capture process gap but does not yet supply discriminating epoch-failure proof. cp36's all501 and old TQA remain historical for their original bytes and cannot accept this new source. At review time root reported the new final all still in progress with the official repeat still failing; no live final-all log, new GREEN, new totals, final primary acceptance or independent new TQA/final-review outcome was read or inferred.
